newsitem.title: USA: R.R. Donnelley, Jesse Jackson to meet Monday.
newsitem.headline: R.R. Donnelley, Jesse Jackson to meet Monday.

text.p: R.R. Donnelley & Sons Co said it expects to meet later Monday morning with civil rights leader Jesse Jackson and the Rainbow/PUSH Action Network to discuss a $500 million racial discrimination lawsuit brought by former employees of the printing company.
"We hope to have a productive meeting," said R.R. Donnelley spokesman William Lowe.
Lowe said the company's senior management will participate in the session.
Last week the company said it learned it was named in a complaint alleging it discriminated against black employees when arranging transfers in 1993 related to a plant closing.
R.R. Donnelley has categorically denied the allegations and said in a statement, "all employees were and continue to be treated fairly and equally, no matter what their position within the company."
It added, "The lawsuit does not and will not change R.R. Donnelley's commitment to diversity and equal opportunity."

Jackson previously met with the chief executive of Texaco Inc over a racial discrimination suit filed by six black employees in 1994. Texaco in November agreed to a $176 million setlement to the suit.
